# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

     3	/// The video pump of a row a bundled encoder writes (`settings.writer`, spec §11 CX-12):
     4	/// the composed frames converted to I420 on the export's video queue and encoded by SVT-AV1
     5	/// on a serial encode queue of its own, whose packets go to a passthrough
     6	/// `AVAssetWriterInput` as `av01` samples.
     7	///
     8	/// **Two queues, one owner each.** The video queue reads, converts and hands each frame on,
     9	/// bounded to three in flight (`slots`) so a slow encoder holds the read back; the encode
    10	/// queue owns the encoder and the input — every `send`, every packet, every append, the
    11	/// flush and `markAsFinished`. Progress is counted by frames SUBMITTED (the encoder's lag
    12	/// is under a second); a cancel is the writer's flag, read before each read, each send and
    13	/// each wait for the input.
    14	///
    15	/// **The finish** runs once on the encode queue, after every frame queued before it: at the
    16	/// end of a clean read, the end of stream and a drain to the last packet; on a stop (a
    17	/// cancel, a failed read, another pump's failure), the end of stream and a drain that
    18	/// discards; after an encoder error, neither. Every exit marks the input finished and
    19	/// leaves the group exactly once. The encoder itself is torn down by `close()`, after
    20	/// `allInputsFinished`, as the reader is (G-17).

    22	    /// The settings' `writer` this pump serves.
    23	    static let writer = "svt_av1"
    24	
    25	    let formatDescription: CMVideoFormatDescription
    26	
    27	    private var encoder: SVTAV1Encoder?
    28	    private let converter: ExportI420Converter
    29	    private let encodeQueue = DispatchQueue(
    30	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.encode", qos: .userInitiated)
    31	    private let range: CMTimeRange
    32	    private let frameDuration: CMTime
    33	    private let slots = DispatchSemaphore(value: 3)
    34	
    35	    // The encode queue's own state.
    36	    private var times: [Int64: CMTime] = [:]
    37	    private var lastTime = CMTime.negativeInfinity
    38	    private var encoderFailed = false
    39	    private var finished = false
    40	
    41	    init(settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize, range: CMTimeRange) throws {

    43	        let speed = settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced
    44	        let rate = settings.videoBitrate.map { max(1, $0) }
    45	            ?? ExportWriter.defaultVideoBitrate(settings, bitsPerPixel: 0.07)

    47	            width: frame.width, height: frame.height, fps: settings.fps, bitsPerSecond: rate,
    48	            speed: speed)

    51	            config = try ReelAV1.config(sequenceHeader: encoder.sequenceHeader)
    52	        } catch {

    60	            fills: ExportWriter.fillsTheBox(settings, canvas: canvas), pool: 3)

    68	    }

    70	    /// Reads `output` to its end on `queue` and encodes it into `input`; `group` is left once
    71	    /// the input is finished. `readFailure` answers the reader's error when the read failed;
    72	    /// `fail` records the first failure; `advance` is each submitted frame's file time.
    73	    func run(
    74	        input: AVAssetWriterInput, output: AVAssetReaderOutput, on queue: DispatchQueue,
    75	        group: DispatchGroup, isStopping: @escaping () -> Bool,
    76	        readFailure: @escaping () -> (any Error)?, fail: @escaping (any Error) -> Void,
    77	        advance: @escaping (CMTime) -> Void
    78	    ) {

    81	            encodeQueue.async {
    82	                self.finish(
    83	                    clean: clean, input: input, group: group, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail)

   127	    // MARK: - The encode queue
   128	
   129	    private func encode(
   130	        _ frame: I420Frame, index: Int64, time: CMTime, input: AVAssetWriterInput,

   134	            converter.recycle(frame)
   135	            slots.signal()
   136	        }
   137	        guard !finished, !encoderFailed, !isStopping(), let encoder else { return }
   138	        do {
   139	            try encoder.send(frame, index: index)
   140	            times[index] = time
   141	            while let packet = try encoder.nextPacket(wait: false) {
   142	                guard write(packet, input: input, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail) else {
   143	                    return
   144	                }
   145	            }
   146	        } catch {
   147	            encoderFailed = true
   148	            fail(error)
   149	        }
   150	    }
   151	
   152	    /// One packet into the file: false once the export cannot go on.
   153	    private func write(
   154	        _ packet: SVTAV1Encoder.Packet, input: AVAssetWriterInput, isStopping: () -> Bool,
   155	        fail: (any Error) -> Void
   156	    ) -> Bool {
   157	        guard !packet.data.isEmpty else { return true }
   158	        var data = packet.data
   159	        guard ReelAV1.stripTemporalDelimiters(&data) else {
   160	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 wrote a packet the core could not read."))
   161	            return false
   162	        }
   163	        guard let time = times.removeValue(forKey: packet.pts), time > lastTime else {
   164	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 wrote a frame out of order."))
   165	            return false
   166	        }
   167	        lastTime = time
   168	        guard let sample = ExportAV1Track.sample(
   169	            data, at: time, duration: frameDuration, format: formatDescription)
   170	        else {
   171	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("An AV1 packet could not be made a sample."))
   172	            return false
   173	        }
   174	        while !input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
   175	            guard !isStopping() else { return false }
   176	            usleep(1000)
   177	        }
   178	        guard input.append(sample) else {
   179	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
   180	            return false
   181	        }
   182	        return true
   183	    }

   185	    /// The one exit: the end of stream and the drain as `clean` and the encoder allow, then
   186	    /// the input finished and the group left, exactly once.
   187	    private func finish(

   210	        }

     2	
     3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
     4	[`README.md`](README.md).
     5	
     6	The road map that makes these is `designs/codec-export.md` (in progress); its spike record
     7	(`## S — the spike`) holds every measurement cited here. CX-1..CX-11 were recorded in C0,
     8	before any code. Each is marked "owner" (the owner's choice, 2026-10-27) or "default" (the
     9	orchestrator's default, which the owner can still change by a new entry here).
    10	
    11	- **CX-1 — The road map: bundled software encoders, four export rows** (owner, 2026-10-27:
    12	  "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Frame Job exports AV1 and VP9 with
    13	  encoders built into the app, as four rows:
    14	  1. AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
    15	  2. AV1 in WebM, with Opus audio;
    16	  3. VP9 in WebM, with Opus audio;
    17	  4. VP9 with alpha in WebM.
    18	
    19	  VP9 in MP4 is not wanted: it works (the spike measured it) but carries no alpha and is less
    20	  efficient than AV1 in MP4, so it does nothing another row does not. AV1 with alpha is not
    21	  wanted because none exists in practice: neither SVT-AV1's nor libaom's API takes an alpha
    22	  input, and the Matroska AV1 mapping defines none. **Risk accepted:** software encoding is
    23	  1.5–5.4× slower than VideoToolbox's HEVC per 1080p frame on the spike's M2 Max and needs
    24	  1.0–2.1 GB, and the app grows by about 5 MB.
    25	
    26	- **CX-2 — AV1 is SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 alone; there is no libaom** (owner). Its three speeds are
    27	  Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (the default) and Smaller file = preset 4. The
    28	  spike measured SVT-AV1 at about 3× libaom's speed at matched quality (SVT 4 ≈ libaom
    29	  good-5/6), and better quality at every matched speed; libaom's best tier (good-3/4) was
    30	  about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. Presets 10 and 12 were within 0–0.7 VMAF
    31	  of HEVC at 2–3× its CPU cost, so they get no row. **Risk accepted:** SVT-AV1's worst frame
    32	  (VMAF 86–88) is lower than libaom's (92), and its memory is higher (1.0–2.1 GB against
    33	  0.5–1.1 GB).
    34	
    35	- **CX-3 — VP9 is libvpx v1.17.0 at `--good` cpu-used 4 with row-mt, one speed** (owner).
    36	  VP9's reason to be on the sheet is web playback and alpha, not efficiency: at matched
    37	  quality it needs 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's bitrate. cpu-used 2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 %
    38	  more time, and rt-8 only matched HEVC, so neither gets a row. **Risk accepted:** one speed,
    39	  so no faster VP9 for a long export.
    40	
    41	- **CX-4 — The encoders are platform-side** (default). Swift calls their C APIs through the
    42	  bridging header (`app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h`); no `rc_*` export wraps them and
    43	  the core never links them, because encoding is sample work and the core does none (spec
    44	  §7). They are arm64, static (each `.a` linked by its full path into the app's one
    45	  executable, never a dylib) and encoder-only (SVT-AV1 `BUILD_DEC=OFF`, libvpx
    46	  `--disable-vp8 --disable-vp9-decoder`). "No ffmpeg dependency in the product" stands: these
    47	  are two encoder libraries, not ffmpeg. **Risk accepted:** the encoders' C APIs become part
    48	  of the Swift side's surface, and an encoder bug crashes the app rather than a helper.
    49	
    50	- **CX-5 — The build policy** (default):
    51	  1. Each library is a pinned release tarball checked by SHA-256, fetched and built by
    52	     `make codecs` and by Xcode's "Build Codecs" pre-build step
    53	     (`tools/codecs/build_codecs.py`), installed into `build/codecs/` and reused while its
    54	     stamp's key (the script's bytes, the pins, the tool versions and the deployment target)
    55	     and every recorded output's digest match.
    56	  2. No library source is in git (about 16.7 MB of tarballs stay out). The tools are cmake
    57	     from Homebrew and the system's perl (`/usr/bin/perl`); no nasm, yasm, meson or ninja.
    58	  3. A downloaded tarball whose digest is not the pin's fails the build, naming both digests,
    59	     and is deleted.
    60	  4. Each library's licence and patent texts ship in the bundle at
    61	     `Contents/Resources/Licenses/<library>/`, copied from the source tree; the
    62	     acknowledgements (#376) list them.
    63	
    64	  **Risk accepted:** cmake on every build machine and the publish runner, network for the
    65	  first fetch, and a clean build of about one to two minutes.
    66	
    67	- **CX-6 — The WebM writer is Rust in `core/`, beside #216-R's reader, not libwebm** (owner).
    68	  Writing container bytes is not sample work, under #216-R's precedent (`deepening.md`): the
    69	  writer decides timestamps, cluster and cue placement and CodecDelay, and touches compressed
    70	  packets only as opaque bytes. It honours spec §7.8's chapters, range and size and #337's
    71	  audio length, so the WebM rows are not a lesser second writer, and it is round-trip tested
    72	  against the reader in `make test`. **Risk accepted:** a new writer to maintain instead of
    73	  Google's proven muxer, and the reader's grid rule and the writer's timing must agree (the
    74	  spike saw libwebm's millisecond times read back off the grid).
    75	
    76	- **CX-7 — Opus comes from AudioToolbox** (default), not libopus. It sits where AAC does:
    77	  after the mix and the loudness gain (`ExportAudioGain`, `ExporterLoudness`). The writer
    78	  builds OpusHead and CodecDelay itself, the pre-skip taken from the converter's `primeInfo`
    79	  (312 frames measured), because Apple's 28-byte cookie is not OpusHead. AV1 in MP4 keeps AAC.
    80	  **Risk accepted:** Apple's VBR came in under the asked rate (72 kb/s for 128 k on a test
    81	  tone), and libopus (+0.32 MB) is the fallback only if a quality or control gap shows up.
    82	
    83	- **CX-8 — HDR** (default): the AV1 rows are 10-bit, with HLG or PQ tagged in both the
    84	  bitstream (the sequence header's colour config) and the container (`colr` in MP4, `Colour`
    85	  in WebM), plus HD-5's HDR10 mastering metadata (`mdcv`/`clli`, WebM's MasteringMetadata).
    86	  They take `hevc_10bit`'s place in H-3's rules. VP9 Profile 2 HDR is a later phase of its
    87	  own, WebM only, because VP9's bitstream carries no transfer function and the container must.
    88	  **Risk accepted:** no player's HDR rendering of these files was measured.
    89	
    90	- **CX-9 — The rate model keeps the bitrate semantics on every row** (default):
    91	  1. `video_bitrate` is the single-pass VBR target (two passes would compose every frame
    92	     twice);
    93	  2. the Quality tiers apply HEVC's 0.6 factor to AV1 and VP9, and "Format default" is HEVC's
    94	     0.07 bits per pixel per frame;
    95	  3. the efficiency goes to the picture, not the file size, because the owner wants quality
    96	     (2026-10-27): SVT 6 measured +2.8 to +4.8 VMAF over HEVC at HEVC's rate;
    97	  4. **risk accepted:** a rate is a target, and single-pass SVT-AV1 undershot it by 14–22 % on
    98	     5 s clips (libvpx overshot by 5–7 %). C1 re-measures on a full-length export. *Result
    99	     (C1):* on the owner's 55 s 1080p30 clip single-pass VBR at Balanced came in at
   100	     0.667–0.670 of the target in six runs, at "Format default" and at High
   101	     (`designs/codec-export.md`, C1); the owner then chose capped constant quality for the
   102	     AV1 rows, CX-13, which replaces (1) and this item there.
   103	
   104	- **CX-10 — On an M1 or M2 the AV1 export still works, but Frame Job cannot preview or
   105	  re-import that file** (default): those Macs have no AV1 decoder, and #216's refusal stands.
   106	  The user guide says so (C1), and playback is a manual check on an M3 or later. **Risk
   107	  accepted:** a user on an M1/M2 exports a file they cannot watch in Frame Job or QuickTime.
   108	
   109	- **CX-11 — The working arrangement** (default): the road map is built in the `codecs`
   110	  worktree, each phase gated and merged on its own. C0 adds no export row and no format bump:
   111	  it records these decisions, opens the road map and builds and links the two libraries.
   112	
   113	- **CX-12 — C1's shape: AV1 in MP4 at 8 bits** (default, recorded in C1 before its code):
   114	  1. **The row.** `av1`, "AV1 (MP4)", after `hevc_10bit` in the table: MP4, codec `av1`, video
   115	     with AAC audio, no alpha, even-sized as every AVFoundation row but `prores_4444` (G-33).
   116	     Its `avf_preset` is `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough`, a record only, because
   117	     AVFoundation still writes the container; a new field, `writer` (`svt_av1`), names the
   118	     encoder route, so `avf_preset: null` keeps meaning the ImageIO writer and no other row
   119	     changes.
   120	  2. **The speed.** `encoder_speed` is `faster`, `balanced` (the default) or `smaller` — SVT-AV1
   121	     preset 8, 6 or 4 (CX-2) — and is refused on a row without encoder speeds, naming the key.
   122	     The sheet's Speed row sits under Format (after Dynamic Range when that is shown); on
   123	     another row it is disabled and shows the last choice, as Quality does, and the choice is
   124	     remembered with the rest of the sheet (`ExportChoice`).
   125	  3. **Keyframes.** A closed GOP (`intra_refresh_type` = `SVT_AV1_KF_REFRESH`), a keyframe at
   126	     least every 2 s (`intra_period_length` = ⌊2·fps⌋ − 1). The sync samples are the
   127	     passthrough `AVAssetWriter`'s own, read from the bitstream: C1 measured that marking every
   128	     sample `NotSync` left the file's sync samples at exactly its KEY_FRAMEs, so the pump
   129	     writes no sync attachment, and `av1_export_proof.py` A5's match of each key-flagged
   130	     packet to a shown KEY_FRAME, both ways, is the guard. The `SVT_AV1_KF_REFRESH` line is
   131	     live only under CX-13's capped CRF: SVT-AV1 v4.2.0 forces KF refresh under single-pass
   132	     VBR (`lap_rc`), and under CRF its FWDKF refresh writes each 2 s refresh as a hidden
   133	     INTRA_ONLY frame (`frame_type` 2, `show_frame` 0, shown later by `show_existing_frame`)
   134	     after one KEY_FRAME, which A5 refuses.
   135	  4. **The container bytes are the core's.** The `av1C` record (built from SVT's sequence
   136	     header OBU), the stripping of temporal delimiters from every packet and the rewrite of
   137	     the written file's `ftyp` to carry `av01` are decided in the core (CX-6's container-bytes
   138	     precedent; `rc_av1_*`). A written file whose `ftyp` cannot take `av01` fails the export.
   139	  5. **The frames.** The compositor's 64RGBAHalf frames are converted on the GPU to BT.709
   140	     video-range I420 (chroma the mean of each 2×2 block); when the export size is not the
   141	     canvas, `MPSImageLanczosScale` scales first, fit or fill per G-33 (c), with black bars.
   142	  6. **SVT-AV1's log** goes through `svt_av1_set_log_callback`: info and debug are dropped,
   143	     warnings and errors become `NSLog("SVT-AV1: …")`.
   144	  7. **HDR projects.** In an HLG project the `av1` row writes the SDR version, by HD-14's
   145	     existing rule for an SDR row; 10-bit and HDR AV1 are C2's (CX-8).
   146	
   147	- **CX-13 — AV1's rate is a soft cap: capped constant quality, quality first** (owner,
   148	  2026-10-27, "Capped constant quality", chosen after C1 measured single-pass VBR at
   149	  0.667–0.670 of its target on a 55 s 1080p clip; then 2026-10-28, "Quality first, soft
   150	  cap"; amends CX-9 (1) and (4) for the AV1 rows, CX-9 (2) and (3) standing):
   151	  1. **The mode.** SVT-AV1 runs capped CRF: `rate_control_mode` 0 with `aq_mode` 2 (what its
   152	     own `--crf` sets), `qp` the CRF, and `max_bit_rate` the cap — the mode SVT-AV1 v4.2.0's
   153	     `EbSvtAv1Enc.h` documents for `max_bit_rate` and `mbr_over_shoot_pct` ("Capped CRF") and
   154	     its `enc_settings.c` refuses outside rate-control mode 0. `mbr_over_shoot_pct` is SVT's
   155	     own default, 50 (`EbSvtAv1Enc.h` "Default is 50", `enc_settings.c`, `Docs/Parameters.md`),
   156	     so the requested rate is a cap the encoder aims under that hard footage may exceed: at
   157	     (3)'s CRFs on the spike's clips the largest whole-file average was **1.254 × the cap**
   158	     (gh5, 25 fps, Faster at Format default; 14 of 45 files over 1 ×, all of them gh5 but one
   159	     real8 at 1.022 ×), with every file at or above HEVC's VMAF (the least margin +0.035).
   160	     **The tolerance:** `av1_export_proof.py` R1 and R2 hold each file of the owner's clip to
   161	     at most 1.30 × the cap (raised from 1.25 × at integration, above the measured 1.254 ×) and to a VMAF at or above `hevc`'s. **Declined (owner, 2026-10-28):
   162	     a strict cap.** At 12 % overshoot every spike file stayed at or under 0.990 × the cap, but
   163	     the cap then lowers the picture while the file is far under it (SVT holds keyframes and
   164	     base-layer frames to a share of each 60-frame window), and the owner's clip at Faster,
   165	     Format default, plateaued under HEVC's 95.469:
   166	
   167	     | Faster, Format default, owner's clip | 12 % overshoot | 50 % overshoot |
   168	     |---|---|---|
   169	     | CRF 24 | 95.055 (0.645 × the cap) | 95.583 (0.729 ×) |
   170	     | CRF 20 | 95.184 (0.703 ×) | 95.919 (0.844 ×) |
   171	     | CRF 16 | 95.348 (0.735 ×) | — |
   172	
   173	     (25 % and 20 % held gh5 to 1.03 × and 0.999 × at the first CRFs; at 10 % the cap
   174	     dropped gh5 at Faster's Medium 0.02–0.08 VMAF under HEVC.)
   175	  2. **The cap** is the rate the row resolves today: `video_bitrate` when asked (the Quality
   176	     popup's tier rate, HEVC's 0.6 factor, CX-9 (2)), else HEVC's 0.07 bits per pixel per
   177	     frame ("Format default"), clamped to SVT's 100,000 kb/s.
   178	  3. **The CRF matches or beats HEVC at HEVC's own rate, so a Quality tier moves it.** The
   179	     encoder sees only the cap, so the CRF is a function of the cap's bits per pixel per frame
   180	     (cap ÷ (width × height × fps)) and the speed: linear between the calibrated points below,
   181	     rounded down (a lower CRF is the better picture), and the end point's CRF beyond either
   182	     end. Each point is the lower of two calibrations, each the highest CRF on its grid at
   183	     which SVT-AV1 at that preset reached VMAF ≥ HEVC's at the point's rate (ffmpeg's libvmaf;
   184	     `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf.py`, `crf_owner.py`, `crf.jsonl`): the spike's three
   185	     8-bit 1080p clips (gh5, promo, real8), SVT-AV1's own encoder against VideoToolbox HEVC
   186	     through ffmpeg, CRF 18–46 in steps of 2; and the owner's 55 s 1080p30 IMG_0018.MOV
   187	     through Frame Job itself, its `av1` export (a copy of the tree reading the CRF from a
   188	     file) against its `hevc` export, both scored against its `prores_422` export, CRF 12–44
   189	     on a grid of 2 to 8. The second was added when `av1_export_proof.py` R1 and R2 found the
   190	     first's CRFs 0.6–1.9 VMAF under the app's HEVC on that clip: the spike's command-line
   191	     encodes of decoded frames score lower than the app's own, by 1.1 VMAF for SVT-AV1 at one
   192	     CRF and 1.6 for HEVC at one rate on that clip, so the first did not transfer.
   193	
   194	     | bits per pixel per frame (the 1080p30 rate) | Faster (8) | Balanced (6) | Smaller file (4) |
   195	     |---|---|---|---|
   196	     | 0.0386 (Low, 2.4 Mb/s) | 40 | 36 | 36 |
   197	     | 0.0579 (Medium, 3.6 Mb/s) | 28 | 30 | 30 |
   198	     | 0.0700 (Format default, 4.35 Mb/s) | 24 | 26 | 26 |
   199	     | 0.0772 (High, 4.8 Mb/s) | 22 | 24 | 24 |
   200	     | 0.1157 (Maximum, 7.2 Mb/s) | 14 | 16 | 16 |
   201	
   202	     The owner's clip binds every point but Faster's Medium, which the spike's promo graphic
   203	     binds (its VMAF saturates near 97.7, so its margins are hundredths of a point), and
   204	     Faster's Low, where both give 40. At (1)'s 50 % the owner's clip held it under the real
   205	     cap (`--rate` on Release, 2026-10-28): Format default 95.570 / 95.632 / 95.506 and High
   206	     95.856 / 96.067 / 95.951 (Faster / Balanced / Smaller file) against `hevc`'s 95.469 and
   207	     95.777, every file 0.48–0.73 × the cap.
   208	  4. **What the user is told.** The guide, the MCP page, the sheet's tier titles and footnote
   209	     ("usually ≤ …") and `export`'s `video_bitrate` description say the rate is a soft cap the
   210	     file usually stays under, and one sentence names the measured overshoot (about 1.25 ×).
   211	     **Risk accepted:** a file's size is no longer predictable from its rate and can exceed
   212	     it; the calibration is four clips at 1080p (other sizes are placed by bits per pixel
   213	     alone), one of them the binding one, so other footage can land a little under HEVC; and
   214	     the owner clip's grid is coarse (Balanced and Smaller file at Low: 36 passed, 44 did not).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Road map "codec-export" C1 — the `av1` row: AV1 in MP4 through the bundled
SVT-AV1 (spec §11 CX-1, CX-2, CX-9, CX-10, CX-12, CX-13).

    python3 tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH] [--rate]
    python3 tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py --mutant NAME

Launches its own instances of the chosen app (`proof_app.py`: `--app`, else
`RC_PROOF_APP`, else Debug; a build older than its inputs is refused) on scratch
sockets, works under `tools/proof/work/av1-export/`, closes every project it opens
with `discard: true` and stops each instance by its own PID. ffprobe and ffmpeg
(Homebrew, with libdav1d) only READ the files: this Mac has no AV1 decoder, so
nothing here imports or plays an AV1 file through Frame Job or AVFoundation.

Rows (`<ID> ok|FAIL — <detail>`, then `scores: n/m`; exit 0 iff all passed):

* Z1 — every instance's log is silent: no `Frame Job: ` line (the parity check),
  no `Svt[` line (SVT's own banner, which CX-12 (6) routes away) and no
  `SVT-AV1: ` line (a warning or error it passed on).
* A1 — `export {preset: av1}` of AV.mov (640 × 360, 30 fps, 5 s) under a text
  clip is done; ffprobe reads video `av1` / `av01` / Main / `yuv420p` /
  640 × 360 and audio `aac` / `mp4a`, and the video lasts 5.0 s ± one frame.
* A2 — the file's compatible brands include `av01`.
* A3a — the bitstream: `-bsf:v trace_headers`' every sequence header has
  `color_description_present_flag` 1, `color_primaries`, `transfer_characteristics`
  and `matrix_coefficients` 1/1/1 and `color_range` 0.
* A3b — the container: the `av01` sample entry's `colr` box, read from the MP4's
  own bytes (moov/trak/mdia/minf/stbl/stsd), is `nclx` 1/1/1 with full_range 0.
* A4 — `ffmpeg -v error` decodes the file with no error line, ffprobe's decoded
  frame count is the range's (150), and `trace_headers` shows no temporal
  delimiter OBU (type 2).
* A5 — A1's file: the first packet is a keyframe (K), the longest K-to-K gap is
  ≤ 2.0 s, the key count is ≤ ceil(duration / 2 s) + 1 with at least one packet
  that is not K, and through `trace_headers` every K packet's shown frame is a
  KEY_FRAME (`frame_type` 0 with `show_frame` 1) and no other packet's is, and
  no packet holds a hidden intra frame (`frame_type` 0 or 2 with `show_frame` 0:
  an open GOP's forward keyframe).
* A6 — a 1920 × 1080, 30 fps, 120 s project (AV.mov 24 times, filling the
  canvas) exported at Balanced, cancelled once its progress is above 0 while it
  encodes — after the loudness measurement's phase, whose progress is the bar's
  first share, so the cancel meets the encoder and not the measurement: the
  status reads `cancelled` within 10 s of `cancel_export`, and no file is at
  the path. (Uncancelled, its 3,600 frames take far longer than 10 s at
  SVT-AV1's ~41–148 fps at 1080p, `designs/codec-export.md`'s spike.)
* A7 — A1's project at each `encoder_speed` (faster, balanced, smaller): each
  done, its answer's `encoder_speed` the one asked, and the three files' sizes
  pairwise more than 1 % apart; `encoder_speed: "fast"` and `encoder_speed` on `h264`
  are each refused naming `encoder_speed`, and nothing is at either path.
* A8 — `size: [640, 480]` on the 640 × 360 canvas is 640 × 480 with the
  picture letterboxed (the top 56 rows' luma ≤ 20, the middle rows' mean above
  20, frame 0's Y plane); `size: "720p"` decodes at 1280 × 720.
* A9 — an in/out export of 1 s to 3 s holds 60 frames.
* S1 — an instance pinned with `screens.py`'s PINS, `-RCDevAppearance light`
  and `FrameJobExportChoice` `{"preset_id":"av1","encoder_speed":"smaller"}`:
  File ▸ Export… shows Format "AV1 (MP4)", the popup after "Speed:" reads
  "Smaller file" and is drawn enabled, and the footnote is
  "AV1 · MP4 · Smaller file".
* S2 — the same pinned to `{"preset_id":"h264"}`: the Speed popup is drawn
  disabled. "Drawn enabled / disabled": the layout dump carries no enabled
  flag, so the popup's darkest pixel is compared with the Format popup's in
  the same light capture — within 40 levels is enabled, more than 60 lighter
  is disabled.
* R1, R2 — only with `--rate` (CX-13's soft-capped CRF): the owner's full-length
  clip `tools/proof/media/owner-sync/IMG_0018.MOV` (1920 × 1080, 30 fps,
  55.27 s) exported once as `prores_422` (the reference), then, R1 at "Format
  default" (no `video_bitrate`: the cap is HEVC's 0.07 bits per pixel per
  frame) and R2 at the sheet's High tier (`video_bitrate` 0.129 × 0.6 to the
  nearest 100 kbps, asked of both), as `hevc` and as `av1` at each speed:
  each `av1` file's video bit rate (ffprobe, the whole file's average) is at
  most 1.25 × the cap (CX-13's soft cap) and its VMAF against the reference
  (ffmpeg's libvmaf, both as 8-bit 4:2:0) is at or above the `hevc` file's.
  Prints each rate, its share of the cap, each VMAF and each encode's frames
  per second. A missing fixture skips R by name; a libvmaf that cannot run is
  a FAIL.

`--mutant NAME` builds a copy of the tree (`tree_copy.make_copy`; `core/` made
the copy's own for a core mutant, `hevc_alpha_proof.own_core`) with each of the
mutant's anchors replaced (each found exactly once), builds its app
(`tree_copy.build_app`), runs every row but R on it (and, for a core mutant,
its `cargo test` file in the copy's core), and exits 1 when exactly the named
rows fail (caught), 0 when none of them does (survived), 3 when they fail
with others beside them, and 2 when the control could not be performed (a
copy, an anchor, a build or a launch).

  td-kept                    the core's strip keeps every temporal delimiter:
                             A4 and `cargo test --test av1_mp4`
  brand-unpatched            the finished file is never branded: A2
  open-gop                   `SVT_AV1_FWDKF_REFRESH` (an open GOP): A5 (hidden
                             INTRA_ONLY frames, one key) and Z1 (SVT-AV1's warning
                             that it set hierarchical levels to 4 for it)
  speed-ignored              SVT's preset fixed at 6: A7
  encode-ignores-cancel      every `isStopping()` in `ExportEncodePump` removed: A6
  speed-on-any-row           the core takes `encoder_speed` on any row: A7 and
                             `cargo test --test export_av1`
  colour-untagged-bitstream  SVT's CICP left unset: A3a
  colour-untagged-container  the format description's colour extensions
                             dropped: A3b

An instrument that cannot run is a FAIL, never an exit.
"""

silent movie has NO audio group (an `.m4a` clip has no video group), so the
solo proof needs two tones it can tell apart by ear and by byte, and the
paste-attributes proof needs one clip that has BOTH groups:

       -ac 2 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -b:a 128k -shortest AV.mov
```

under it.) `phase2_proof.py` also runs `ffmpeg` at proof time, to decode
each `audio_m4a` export to raw PCM

# Core Graphics draws Core Media 709's γ curve with a slope limit of 16: its decode is
# max(s/16, s^γ) (measured in H-2, `hdr_probe.swift` P6), and so is the lift's.
CM709_TOE = 16.0
# hdr H-3 (#277, spec §11 HD-4, HD-5, HD-7, HD-14): the deliverables' rows and numbers.
# The SDR version's knee and white (HD-14 (a)), and the SDR grey at the knee, below which
# the version is the round trip; the video rows, the three that carry HDR, the tags each
# picture is written with, HD-5's HDR10 side data as ffprobe names it, and the menu item.
H3_ROWS = {"DT", "DP", "DV", "DI", "DE", "DR", "DS", "DM", "DX"}
SDR_KNEE = 0.9
SDR_WHITE = PQ_WHITE / PQ_REFERENCE
SDR_KNEE_GREY = 0.9477
VIDEO_ROWS = ["h264", "hevc", "hevc_10bit", "hevc_alpha", "prores_422", "prores_4444", "gif",
              "apng"]
HDR_ROWS = ["hevc_10bit", "prores_422", "prores_4444"]
PICTURE_TAGS = {"sdr": "bt709/bt709/bt709", "hlg": "bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020",
                "pq": "bt2020nc/smpte2084/bt2020"}
HDR10_SIDE = {"red_x": "34000/50000", "red_y": "16000/50000", "green_x": "13250/50000",
              "green_y": "34500/50000", "blue_x": "7500/50000", "blue_y": "3000/50000",
              "white_point_x": "15635/50000", "white_point_y": "16450/50000",
              "min_luminance": "50/10000", "max_luminance": "10000000/10000",
              "max_content": "1000", "max_average": "0"}
SDR_VERSION_MENU = ["View", "Show SDR Version"]
DE_H264_BITRATE = 50_000_000
# hdr H-4 (#277, spec §11 HD-8, HD-15): the scopes' rows. SI holds every SDR project's scope
# JSON and sentences to DIR's; the rest read an HLG project's.
H4_ROWS = {"SI", "SW", "SV", "SS", "SD", "SP"}

def ramp_sdr_misses(frame, source, oracle, tag, bound, misses, step=64, matrix="bt2020nc"):
    """The grey row every `step`th column against `oracle(R'G'B')` within `bound`; the
    largest miss in levels of 255."""
    worst = 0.0
    for x in range(0, W, step):
        want = oracle(source.rgb(x, GREY_ROW, matrix))
        got = frame.px(x, GREY_ROW)
        gap = max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(got, want))
        worst = max(worst, gap)
        if gap > bound and len(misses) < 12:
            misses.append(f"{tag} x={x} got {[round(v, 5) for v in got]} want "
                          f"{[round(v, 5) for v in want]} ({gap * 255:.2f}/255)")
    return worst * 255


def code_column(source, code):
    """The first grey-row column whose luma code is `code`, or None."""
    return next((x for x in range(W) if source.codes(x, GREY_ROW)[0] == code), None)


def run_dt(client, state):
    """DT: every video row of an HLG project at its default and each accepted
    dynamic_range, tagged as the picture it writes; no Dolby Vision in any HEVC file."""
    misses, figures = [], []
    doc = hlg_doc(client, "dt", [fixture("hlg")])
    for preset in VIDEO_ROWS:
        ranges = [None, "hlg", "pq", "sdr"] if preset in HDR_ROWS else [None, "sdr"]
        for asked in ranges:
            tag = f"dt-{preset}-{asked or 'default'}"
            extra = {"dynamic_range": asked} if asked else {}
            path, got = export_as(doc, tag, preset, **extra)
            picture = asked or ("hlg" if preset in HDR_ROWS else "sdr")
            said = reply(got).get("dynamic_range")
            if path is None:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: {got.get('error', 'no file')}")
                continue
            if said != picture:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: the result's dynamic_range {said!r}, not {picture!r}")
            if preset in ("gif", "apng"):
                figures.append(f"{tag}: written ({path.stat().st_size} bytes)")
                continue
            read = tags(stream(path))
            line = f"{tag}: {read}"
            if read != PICTURE_TAGS[picture]:
                misses.append(f"{tag}: {read}, not {PICTURE_TAGS[picture]}")
            if preset.startswith("hevc"):
                record, rpu = dovi(path)
                line += f", DOVI record {record}, RPU {rpu}"
                if record or rpu:
                    misses.append(f"{tag}: Dolby Vision")
            figures.append(line)
    state["dt_closed"] = doc.close()
    check("DT every video row of an HLG project (the hlg ramp, 1 s) at its default and each "
          "accepted dynamic_range: bt709 ×3 for the SDR version, bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020 "
          "for hlg, bt2020nc/smpte2084/bt2020 for pq, the result naming it; no DOVI record or "
          "RPU in any HEVC file; gif and apng written", not misses,
          f"failed {misses or 'none'}\n       " + "\n       ".join(figures))


def run_dp(client, state):
    """DP: the three 10-bit rows at pq carry HD-5's mastering display and content light
    level; prores_422's decoded grey row = the PQ oracle ±2/1023."""
    misses, figures = [], []
    path = fixture("hlg")
    source = yuv_frames(path, W, H) if path else None
    doc = hlg_doc(client, "dp", [path])
    outs = {preset: export_as(doc, f"dp-{preset}", preset, dynamic_range="pq")
            for preset in HDR_ROWS}
    state["dp_closed"] = doc.close()
    for preset, (out, got) in outs.items():
        if out is None:
            misses.append(f"{preset}: {got.get('error', 'no file')}")
            continue
        found = side_all(out)
        figures.append(f"{preset}: {tags(stream(out))}; side data {found}")
        wrong = {k: found.get(k) for k, v in HDR10_SIDE.items() if found.get(k) != v}
        if wrong:
            misses.append(f"{preset}: {wrong}")
    out = outs["prores_422"][0]
    frames = yuv_frames(out, W, H, 16) if out else None
    if frames is None or source is None:
        misses.append("prores_422's frames or the fixture did not decode")
    else:
        worst = 0.0
        for x in range(0, W, 8):
            want = pq_version(source[0].rgb(x, GREY_ROW, "bt2020nc"))
            got = frames[15].rgb(x, GREY_ROW, "bt2020nc")
            gap = max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(got, want))
            worst = max(worst, gap)
            if gap > 2 * LEVEL and len(misses) < 12:
                misses.append(f"prores_422 x={x} {[round(v, 5) for v in got]} want "
                              f"{[round(v, 5) for v in want]}")
        figures.append(f"prores_422's grey row against the PQ oracle: largest miss "
                       f"{levels(worst):.3f}/1023")
    check("DP prores_422, prores_4444 and hevc_10bit at pq: each file's side data P3-D65 "
          "(red 34000/50000 …, white 16450/50000), min_luminance=50/10000 max_luminance="
          "10000000/10000, max_content=1000 max_average=0; prores_422's decoded grey row = the "
          "PQ oracle ±2/1023", not misses,
          f"failed {misses or 'none'}\n       " + "\n       ".join(figures))

docs/guide/export.md:47:| AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | The smallest delivery file, encoded by the AV1 encoder built into Frame Job. 8-bit. Slower to export than HEVC. See [Speed](#speed). |
docs/guide/export.md:73:- **Even dimensions.** H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit, AV1 and ProRes 422 need them, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. ProRes 4444, GIF and APNG keep an odd edge.
docs/guide/export.md:82:The **Speed** row sits under Format (under Dynamic Range in an HDR project). It is live only on **AV1 (MP4)**; on every other format it is greyed out and keeps your last choice.
docs/guide/export.md:251:Only HEVC 10-bit, ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR. On every other video format, AV1 included, the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).
docs/guide/export.md:313:- AV1 is 8-bit only. Its file size is not known in advance: the file usually comes in well under the rate, but very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it.

content.content:
## HDR projects

In an HDR (HLG) project the sheet has a **Dynamic Range** row under Format:

| Choice | What the file holds |
|---|---|
| **HDR (HLG)** | The HLG master. The default. |
| **HDR10 (PQ)** | An HDR10 file with fixed mastering metadata. |
| **SDR version** | The project converted to SDR. |

Only HEVC 10-bit, ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 can carry HDR. On every other video format, AV1 included, the row is greyed out on **SDR version**, which is what those formats write. What each choice contains, and how the SDR version is made, is in [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md#exporting-hdr).

## Transparency

A canvas whose background is transparent (the **Background** row in the Document tab's Appearance section; see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#appearance)) keeps its transparency only in **ProRes 4444**, **HEVC with Alpha** and **Animated PNG**. When the format carries an alpha channel, the footnote ends in "alpha". Every other format composites the picture onto black. A GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so it is not one of the three.

While the canvas background is transparent, the Document tab says how many formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 3 export formats." These are the three formats above.

## Chapters

resolver gives each of the three 10-bit rows — `hevc_10bit`, `prores_422`,
`prores_4444` — `"color": "hlg"` (`ExportSettings.color`), and `videoSettings`
then tags the file BT.2020 primaries, the HLG transfer and the BT.2020 matrix
(ffprobe `bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020`), HEVC with
`kVTHDRMetadataInsertionMode_None`, so VideoToolbox adds no Dolby Vision
configuration or RPU of its own (choice 5a). Every other video row is refused
in its own sentence — `h264 cannot carry an HLG project's picture; export it
as hevc_10bit, prores_422 or prores_4444` — until H-3's SDR version; an audio
row is unchanged, and every SDR project's settings are the text they were.
`render_frame` and Save Frame… read every frame of an HLG project through the
reader (`DeepVideoFrame.reads`, whatever the format) and label it
`itur_2100_HLG` (`FrameWriter.hlgSpace`, kept by `labelled`): a 16-bit PNG
that ImageIO writes with a `cICP` chunk 9/18/0/1, or a 10-bit HEIC; JPEG is
refused (`JPEG cannot carry an HLG project's picture; save the frame as PNG or
HEIC`). The eyedropper and Pick from Canvas read such a frame relabelled sRGB
(`FrameWriter.pickable`), at its code values.

**The deliverables (hdr H-3, §11 HD-4, HD-5, HD-14).** H-2's refusals are
gone. The override `dynamic_range` (`"hlg"`, `"pq"` or `"sdr"`; any other
value refused, `export dynamic_range must be "hlg", "pq" or "sdr", not …`) is
read by `export_overrides.rs` and resolved per row by `dynamic_range.rs`
(`Project::deliverable`): an HLG project's 10-bit rows default to `hlg` and
take all three; its other video rows (`h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `av1`, `gif`,
`apng`) write `sdr`, refusing `hlg` and `pq` (`{id} is 8-bit and writes the
SDR version; export dynamic_range "{x}" as hevc_10bit, prores_422 or
prores_4444`); an SDR project refuses `hlg` and `pq` (`dynamic_range "{x}"
needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first`) and takes `sdr` as
nothing; an audio row reads it and ignores it. The settings' `color` names
the picture (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`) in an HLG project only, and
`rc_export_presets` marks the three 10-bit rows `"hdr": true`
(`ExportPreset.carriesHDR`). `Exporter.export` publishes the asked options

content.content:
In an HDR (HLG) project, the export sheet gets a **Dynamic Range:** row under **Format**. It decides what the 10-bit formats write:

| Item | What the file holds | Default |
|---|---|---|
| HDR (HLG) | The BT.2100 HLG master, Dolby Vision off | Yes |
| HDR10 (PQ) | BT.2100 PQ, mastered at 1,000 cd/m² | |
| SDR version | The SDR version, Rec. 709 | |

- The row is live only on **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)**, **ProRes 422 (MOV)** and **ProRes 4444 (MOV)**. On every other video format it is disabled and shows **SDR version**, because those formats always write the SDR version: H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, Animated GIF and Animated PNG.
- An HDR10 file carries fixed HDR10 metadata: a P3 D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. Its picture never goes above 1,000 cd/m², so the metadata is always accurate. The Media tab's HDR10 Peak describes a *source* file and does not change this.
- The choice applies to that one sheet only. It is not remembered for the next export or saved in an export preset.
- An SDR project's export sheet has no Dynamic Range row.

For formats, sizes and the export queue, see [Export](export.md).

*Agents:* `export` with `dynamic_range` set to `"hlg"`, `"pq"` or `"sdr"`. `hlg` and `pq` are refused on an 8-bit preset ("… is 8-bit and writes the SDR version …") and in an SDR project ("… needs an HLG project; set_canvas output \"hlg\" first"). `export` answers an `export_id` at once; once `export_status` reports the job `done`, its `dynamic_range` names the picture that was written (`hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`).

## Precision and bit depth

- **16-bit float compositing.** Every frame is composited at 16-bit float, and every video source is decoded at full depth. Gradients from a 10-bit camera file survive grading.
- **10-bit exports.** HEVC 10-bit (Main 10), ProRes 422 and ProRes 4444 keep that depth. H.264, HEVC and HEVC with Alpha are 8-bit.
- **Deep stills.** A still deeper than 8 bits per channel, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC, is drawn at 16-bit float. An 8-bit still is drawn as before.
- **Saved and rendered frames.** **File ▸ Save Frame…** writes a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC when the frame shows a deep still or deep video, and in every HDR (HLG) project. JPEG, Animated GIF and Animated PNG are always 8-bit.
- **Reversed clips.** A reversed clip's backwards copy is rendered at 10 bits, at the source's exact size, with the source's own colour labels. That means an HDR or log clip still reads correctly when reversed. See [Speed](speed.md).
- **What stays 8-bit.** Text, shapes, captions, graphics, thumbnails and screen recordings are 8-bit. In an HDR (HLG) project they are still lifted to HDR reference white.

`audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` and `apng`. There is no frame-rate
argument: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and
25 fps for `apng`. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the
format's extension is added when the path has none. `peak_dbtp` without
`loudness_lufs` is refused. `dynamic_range` `hlg` or `pq` is refused outside
`hevc_10bit`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`, and in an SDR project.
`encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`) is `av1`'s alone and is
refused on every other preset; the done answer names it. On `av1`,

content.content:
* Side data attached to decoded frames may come from several sources:
     * 1. coded_side_data, which the decoder will for certain types translate
     *    from packet-type to frame-type and attach to frames;
     * 2. side data attached to an AVPacket sent for decoding (same
     *    considerations as above);
     * 3. extracted from the coded bytestream.
     * The first two cases are supplied by the caller and typically come from a
     * container.
     *
     * This array configures decoder behaviour in cases when side data of the

# Objections

## 1
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** The `av1-not-hdr` mutant is listed as failing only H1 (plus `cargo test --test dynamic_range`). Removing `"av1"` from `HDR_ROWS` also fails H2, H4 and S3. `run_mutant` treats any failing row outside the named set as "caught, not exactly" and exits 3, so the spec's own pass condition ("each of the 9 mutants exits 1 … exactly its named rows failing") cannot be met.
- **Evidence:** `tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py:896-903` exits 1 only when `sorted(named) == failing`, and otherwise exits 3. Under the mutant, `core/src/dynamic_range.rs:82` no longer matches `av1`, so `deliverable` refuses `hlg`/`pq` for it (lines 85-91). That breaks three more rows. H2 (`av1` at `pq`) is refused. H4's HLG-doc exports at `hlg` and `pq` are refused. S3 also fails: `export_table.rs:564-565` no longer emits `"hdr": true` for `av1`, so the sheet's Dynamic Range popup is not "HDR (HLG)" and enabled. H5 still passes, because its sentence is a literal string.
- **Suggested change:** List `av1-not-hdr`'s expected rows as H1, H2, H4, S3 and `cargo-dynamic_range`.

## 2
- **Risk category:** correctness
- **Claim:** H2's bitstream check reads HDR10 from "the first frame decoded by libdav1d". With this Mac's FFmpeg, though, the decoder copies the container's `mdcv`/`clli` onto decoded frames whenever the bitstream has none. So `pq-no-bitstream-metadata` (the parse calls removed) still leaves mastering and light-level side data on frame 0, with values inside H2's tolerances, and the mutant survives.
- **Evidence:** `ffmpeg -version` is 9.0.2. `/opt/homebrew/include/libavcodec/avcodec.h:1890-1906` says: "Side data attached to decoded frames may come from several sources: 1. coded_side_data, which the decoder will for certain types translate from packet-type to frame-type and attach to frames … By default it will be the bytestream side data". Bytestream data only wins when it exists. With the OBUs removed, the container's `/50000` and `/10000` values are attached instead, and they meet "within 1/50000", "1000 ± 1/256" and "0.005 ± 1/16384" exactly.
- **Suggested change:** Make H2 read the OBUs from a source with no container metadata. Either decode `ffmpeg -i <file> -c:v copy -f obu` output and require its frame side data, or require libdav1d's own units on frame 0 (chromaticities over 65536, max luminance over 256, min over 16384), which the container's `/50000` and `/10000` rationals cannot satisfy.

## 3
- **Risk category:** under-scope
- **Claim:** Step 9 re-checks the CRF table only against the owner's clip. One cell, Faster at Medium, is bound by the spike's promo clip, not the owner's. That cell is never re-checked at 10 bits against the new `hevc_10bit` comparator, yet CX-14 (6) will record the whole table as checked against `hevc_10bit`.
- **Evidence:** `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md:182-186` says "each point is the lower of two calibrations". Lines 202-204 add "The owner's clip binds every point but Faster's Medium, which the spike's promo graphic binds (its VMAF saturates near 97.7, so its margins are hundredths of a point)". With margins of hundredths of a VMAF point, changing both the AV1 bit depth and the comparator can flip that cell, and `crf_owner.py --ten-bit` never encodes the promo clip.
- **Suggested change:** Do one of two things. Either re-run the Faster/Medium cell on the spike's promo clip at 10 bits against a 10-bit HEVC encode (and lower it the same way if it falls short), or have CX-14 (6) say that cell's spike half still stands at 8 bits against 8-bit HEVC.

verdict: revise

The verdict is **revise**: I wrote three objections to `/Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/codecs-c2/02-objections.md`. The first two would make the spec's own verification fail, or let a mutant pass without being caught.

1. **correctness: the `av1-not-hdr` mutant lists the wrong rows.** The spec expects only H1 and `cargo test --test dynamic_range` to fail. With `"av1"` taken out of `HDR_ROWS`, three more rows fail:
   - H2 fails because `av1` at `pq` is refused.
   - H4 fails because its `hlg` and `pq` exports are refused.
   - S3 fails because `export_table.rs:564` no longer marks `av1` with `"hdr": true`.

   `av1_export_proof.py:896-903` exits 3 ("caught, not exactly") whenever rows outside the named set fail. So the pass condition "each mutant exits 1" cannot be met. Fix: list H1, H2, H4, S3 and `cargo-dynamic_range` for this mutant.

2. **correctness: the `pq-no-bitstream-metadata` mutant survives H2.** The FFmpeg on this Mac is 9.0.2. Its decoder attaches the container's `mdcv`/`clli` to decoded frames whenever the bitstream carries none (`/opt/homebrew/include/libavcodec/avcodec.h:1890-1906`). H2 reads HDR10 from "the first frame decoded by libdav1d", so with the OBUs removed it still finds the container's values, and those are within all of H2's tolerances. Fix: decode a copy with no container (`-c:v copy -f obu`), or require libdav1d's own units on frame 0: chromaticities over 65536, maximum luminance over 256, minimum over 16384.

3. **under-scope: one CRF cell is never re-checked at 10 bits.** Step 9 recalibrates against the owner's clip only. Faster at Medium is the one cell that clip doesn't set; the spike's promo clip does, by margins of hundredths of a VMAF point (`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md:202-204`). Fix: re-run that cell on the promo clip at 10 bits against a 10-bit HEVC encode, or have CX-14 (6) say that half of the cell still stands at 8 bits.

I also checked and found no problem in:
- the core's `av1C` parser, which already handles high bit depth;
- SVT reading 10-bit input with strides in samples;
- the parse function's string format, which matches `OutputTransform`'s blobs;
- the frames reaching the pump as HLG/PQ BT.2020 values driven by `settings.color`;
- A8's 8-bit decode.

One risk I left out because I can't prove it: H4's mean-difference threshold of 6 codes may be too loose to catch `matrix-709-in-hdr` on the test card. My estimate is about 17 luma codes of difference in saturated red, but 0 in grey areas.
